reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it teaches viewers how to plan, produce, title, and grow a YouTube channel, with earning discussed as channel monetization rather than an investment or payment-based offer. The hacking-related wording is presented as an attention-grabbing title or thumbnail example, while the requests to like, share, and subscribe are ordinary engagement prompts rather than conditions for receiving money, submitting data, or joining a financial scheme.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
One of the most crucial steps you should make before creating your own channel is to plan your content.
Get yourself the right equipment.
Commit yourself to posting on your channel at least three times a week.
The titles of your video should be short and intriguing to make the viewers interested.

opening.argument: The presentation links an income promise to audience participation. The title foregrounds making money, while the video closes by directing viewers to engage with the channel and select additional videos. That combination turns general advice into a solicitation for clicks, continued viewing, and subscription-driven growth: the audience is encouraged to perform the actions that increase the channel’s reach while the headline promises financial gain. Although no deposit is requested, the proposed benefit is still money, and the requested engagement is the mechanism presented for building the channel that supposedly earns it.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
If you learned something new today, then give this video a like and share it with a friend.
We have over 2,000 cool videos for you to check out.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the engagement prompts ordinary does not resolve the central linkage. The title places money in the promise, while the ending asks viewers to like, share, and continue watching. The material therefore encourages audience actions that expand the channel’s distribution, even though it never explains a reliable basis for the promised earnings. Advice about planning and equipment does not eliminate the promotional solicitation created by that pairing.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
give this video a like and share it with a friend
pick the left or right video, click on it, and enjoy

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The money reference is framed as channel monetization, not a payment offered to viewers. The content describes planning and production steps, including equipment, publishing, and presentation; it does not say that liking, sharing, or clicking produces money for the audience. The engagement request is a conventional closing prompt, and the quoted material fails to show a claim, registration flow, or financial transaction directed at viewers.

citations.quote: plan your content
Get yourself the right equipment.
Commit yourself to posting on your channel at least three times a week.

opening.argument: Several signals make the money framing unusually promotional. The headline promises to start a channel and make money, the description emphasizes a platform with more than 1.8 billion users, and the material repeatedly stresses clicks, recommendations, watch time, and subscriber growth. It also supplies multiple outside video links and ends by directing viewers toward more content. None of these facts proves a payout scheme alone, but together they present scale, reach, and easy growth as reasons to pursue the promised income, without establishing that earnings are likely or that the recommended tactics reliably produce them.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
YouTube has more than 1.8 billion users
Such channels are much more successful and get significantly more recommended views.
We have over 2,000 cool videos for you to check out.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of a deposit request is not the only relevant warning sign. The material combines a money headline with claims about recommendation, popularity, and a large audience, then channels viewers toward additional videos. Those claims create urgency to pursue growth while leaving the practical likelihood of income unsubstantiated. Calling the links ordinary does not change that they extend the promotional funnel beyond the central video.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
gain popularity
Other videos you might like:
pick the left or right video, click on it, and enjoy

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited signals show audience-growth advice, not deceptive financial inducement. The material expressly discusses content planning, equipment, editing, upload frequency, thumbnails, and watch time. It does not promise a guaranteed return, specify an amount, or ask viewers to pay, invest, or submit information. External links are identified as other videos, so the evidence does not establish a money-earning claim directed at the viewer.

citations.quote: plan your content
Get yourself the right equipment.
The titles of your video should be short and intriguing
Making long videos can help you to improve watch time.

opening.argument: The instructional format functions as promotion for a channel-growth system. It tells viewers to pursue trending subjects, post at least three times weekly, optimize thumbnails and titles for clicks, use end screens, collaborate for subscribers, and keep watching related material. The title then attaches “make money” to that system. Framed this way, the content is not merely neutral education: it steers viewers toward repeated participation in an attention-and-subscription funnel while presenting monetization as the expected destination. The practical advice may be real, but it does not substantiate the financial outcome being used to attract attention.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
Commit yourself to posting on your channel at least three times a week.
Remember to add end screens
You can also add your channel's logo
We have over 2,000 cool videos for you to check out.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational label does not prevent promotional function. The advice is specifically organized around clicks, recommendations, subscribers, end screens, and continued viewing, while the headline supplies the financial incentive. The question is not whether individual production tips exist; it is whether those tips are being used to steer participation toward a monetization promise. The evidence supports that promotional reading.

citations.quote: How to Start a YouTube Channel And Make Money
more people can relate to it, the more they'll click on your videos

don't go changing the channel just yet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The advice is operational instruction for running a channel, and the growth tactics are directly relevant to that subject. The quoted material does not promise viewers guaranteed earnings or ask them to buy access, deposit funds, recruit others, or claim a reward. A title about making money can describe creator monetization without turning the tutorial into a solicitation for the audience. The promotion theory therefore adds an inference the evidence does not establish.
